newsitem.title: USA: Rhode Island voters approve $230 mln of bonds.
newsitem.headline: Rhode Island voters approve $230 mln of bonds.

text.p: Rhode Island approved nearly $230 million of bonds in five separate initiatives, though they rejected two acts that would have let the state issue $23.5 million more, a state official said on Wednesday.
"Five of the seven passed and two did not," said Steve Klamkin, a spokesman for the state Treasurer.

Precisely when the bonds might be sold was not immediately available. "With regard to the five that passed, by law we have seven years to issue these bonds unless the time is extended by the General Assembly, and the questions are in the capital budget which the governor will submit to the legislature early next year," Klamkin said.
He added, "We do intend to parse it out so it won't increase the state's indebtedness."

Nancy Mayer, the Republican state treasurer, will serve the last two years of her four-year term, after failing to win a bid for the U.S. Senate to Jack Reed, he added. Klamkin noted that Mayer has said she does not plan to run for a second term as state Treasurer.
The following five initiatives, phrased as questions were approved.
--Question 1 - $80 million of general obligation bonds for transportation projects.
--Question 2 - $40 million of general obligation bonds for telecommujications at publci colleges.
--Question 3 - $33 million of general obligation bonds for higher education facilities.
--Question 4 - $72 million of general obligation bonds for Quonset Point/Davisville development.
--Question 5 - $4 million of general obligation bonds for purchase of land to protect natural resources.
However, the voters turned down the following two questions, Klamkin said.
--Question 6 - $5 million of general obligation bonds for environmental remediation revolving loans.

--Question 7 - $18.5 million of general obligation bonds for the repair and renovation of state owned facilities to assure individuals with disabilities accessibility to services and employment opportunities.
